description: Fix four self-defeating workflow recovery defects: rebase conflict handler retrySelf loop, dead conflictMode config, post-rebase push --force-with-lease failure on dynamic branches, and non-idempotent archive-change directory naming across retries.

tasks.title: Remove rebase conflict handler retrySelf and dead conflictMode config
tasks.description: In mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml, remove `retrySelf: true` from the rebase `when: conflict` recovery handler (so the resolve-rebase-conflicts agent's completed rebase is preserved and the flow continues to recover:push instead of re-running recover:rebase which aborts the agent's work) and remove the dead `conflictMode: task` field from the recover:rebase `with` block (the rebase action never reads it). Update the server-side workflow profile assertion tests to reflect the corrected config: assert the conflict handler has NO retrySelf, and assert the rebase `with` has NO conflictMode. No runner code changes are required.
acceptanceCriteria: mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml: the `when: conflict` handler under recover:rebase.recovery has no `retrySelf` key
mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml: the recover:rebase `with` block has no `conflictMode` key
mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml: the parent base-moved handler still has `retrySelf: true` (only the inner conflict handler loses it)
MohistPrIssueWorkflowProfileSpecs.cs: the conflict-handler assertion no longer expects retrySelf==true (asserts absent/false)
MohistPrIssueWorkflowProfileSpecs.cs: the recover:rebase `with` assertion no longer expects conflictMode (asserts absent)
`npm test` (server) passes with the updated profile assertions
tasks.output: Corrected mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml recovery block + updated MohistPrIssueWorkflowProfileSpecs.cs assertions
tasks.notes: Decision 1 + Decision 3. Pure config/test change; the rebase action never reads conflictMode and the agent prompt already completes the rebase. The base-moved handler's own retrySelf (retry of merge-pr) is intentionally kept. Confirm mohist-default.workflow.yaml has no conflictMode to sync (design confirms it does not).

tasks.title: Add force mode to push action and switch post-rebase recovery push to --force
tasks.description: Add a boolean `force` input to the mohist/push action (packages/runner/src/actions/push.ts): when `force === true`, emit a bare `--force` and skip the ls-remote lease probe entirely (no tracking-ref dependency). `force` wins over `forceWithLease` if both are set. Record `force` in the push output JSON alongside the existing `forceWithLease` field. Then switch only the `recover:push` task under the base-moved handler in mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml from `forceWithLease: true` to `force: true`. Leave the check-stage push and the pr-checks-failed recovery push on `forceWithLease: true`. Update runner push tests for the new force mode and server profile assertions for the switched recover:push.
acceptanceCriteria: push.ts: `with.force === true` emits `push --force <remote> <refspec>` with no preceding `ls-remote` call
push.ts: when both `force` and `forceWithLease` are set, `force` wins (bare --force, no ls-remote probe)
push.ts: `force` input absent/false preserves existing forceWithLease/default behavior exactly (no regression)
push.ts: the output JSON includes a `force` boolean field reflecting the mode used
mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml: the base-moved handler's recover:push uses `force: true` and does NOT set `forceWithLease`
mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml: the pr-checks-failed handler's recover:push still uses `forceWithLease: true` (unchanged)
push.spec.ts: covers force mode (bare --force, no ls-remote), force-wins-over-forceWithLease, and existing forceWithLease tests still pass
MohistPrIssueWorkflowProfileSpecs.cs: recoverPushBaseMoved asserts `force`==true and no longer asserts forceWithLease on that task; recoverPushPrChecks still asserts forceWithLease==true
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner`, `npm test -w packages/runner`, and `npm test` (server) all pass
tasks.output: push.ts with force input + force-mode push tests + switched recover:push YAML + updated server profile assertions
tasks.notes: Decision 2. Depends on T-001 because both edit the same YAML file and same server test file region; sequential execution avoids merge conflicts. Rationale: mohist/run-<runId> is single-owner with no remote-tracking ref, so --force-with-lease always fails and is misclassified as base-moved; --force bypasses that. The existing `looksLikeNonFastForward` matching of 'stale info' becomes irrelevant for this push path.

tasks.title: Make archive-change idempotent across retries via mid-execution runtime variable write
tasks.description: Add a mid-execution runtime-variable write helper to the runner action infrastructure: extend ActionContext (packages/runner/src/core/types.ts) with a method that persists a workflow runtime variable immediately via the existing ServerConnection.patchRunVars RPC, and wire it in baseContext() (packages/runner/src/runtime/executor.ts) as a closure over the connection. This write is immediate/best-effort and NOT rolled back on later task failure (distinct from declarative setVars which only fires post-success). Then rewrite archiveChangeAction (packages/runner/src/actions/openspec.ts): before computing/moving the archive directory, check context.variables for a persisted archive name under a reserved internal key (e.g. _actions.archiveChange.destination keyed by sourceName); if present reuse it, otherwise compute the date-prefixed name and persist it BEFORE calling moveChangeDir/uniqueDestination. This makes findExistingArchive locate the already-archived directory on a cross-day retry instead of failing with missing-source.
acceptanceCriteria: ActionContext has a method (e.g. setRuntimeVar/writeVars) that calls connection.patchRunVars immediately during execution, before task completion
baseContext() wires the helper as a closure over this.connection.patchRunVars(workflowRunId, vars, signal)
The mid-execution write is NOT deferred to task completion and is NOT rolled back if the task later fails (documented contract)
archiveChangeAction reads the persisted archive name from context.variables on entry; if present, reuses it as archivePrefix and skips date recomputation
archiveChangeAction persists the computed archive name to the server BEFORE moveChangeDir/uniqueDestination on first execution

On a simulated cross-day retry (different wall-clock date) where a prior execution persisted the name and moved the directory, archiveChangeAction reuses the persisted name, findExistingArchive locates the archived directory, and the action succeeds (no missing-source failure)
On a simulated retry where a prior execution persisted the name but failed AFTER the write and BEFORE the move, the action reuses the name and proceeds normally

openspec.spec.ts: added cross-day idempotency test using a fake ServerConnection capturing patchRunVars calls; existing archive-change tests still pass (adapt archiveContext to provide the new helper/fake connection)
Reserved internal key uses a leading-underscore namespaced prefix that does not collide with user-declared variables
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass
mohist-default.workflow.yaml and mohist-github-pr.workflow.yaml need no archive-change `with` changes (the runner fix is transparent to both profiles)
tasks.output: ActionContext mid-execution write helper + baseContext wiring + idempotent archiveChangeAction + runner tests for cross-day retry and write-survives-failure
tasks.notes: Decision 4 + Decision 5. Fully independent of T-001/T-002 (different package: runner core/runtime/actions + runner tests, no server YAML overlap). Open questions from design: (a) patchRunVars failure policy — lean hard-fail-as-retry-safe so budget:3 re-attempts the write before the irreversible move; (b) helper signature — lean writeVars(vars) for symmetry with setVars/patchRunVars, single-key archive use case still reads cleanly; (c) internal key enforcement — runner-side convention sufficient for the closed action set. Already-archived directories from the old date-prefix scheme remain valid: findExistingArchive still matches them when the persisted name is absent on a first run.
